We'll move right into some comments with respect to final budget day.
Thank you to Council, staff, those in the audience and members of the viewing public for joining us today for our 2025 final budget day.
For the second year in a row, this budget process has continued to take a collaborative approach between Council and staff,
informed by community priorities and recognizing changes made two years ago in provincial legislation requiring that it be presented as a mayor's budget.
As Council knows, the draft 2025 budget was presented during two financing corporate services committee meetings on November 18th and November 25th,
developed by our city staff team and led by our finance budget team.
I want to again thank Ward Councillor Scott Davey, Chair of our Finance and Corporate Services Committee,
for officially proposing the 2025 budget on my behalf at a special council meeting
on December 2, 2024, when I couldn't be here for family reasons and for his leadership throughout
the process. In fact, this is, I think now, 13 budgets that Chair Davey has chaired on behalf of
of the City. Thank you to my colleagues, Council and staff for your support and understanding
during this busy but personally difficult time. I truly appreciate it.
The purpose of today's special Council meeting was to consider any amendments that members
of Council may have related to the Mayor's budget. Members of Council were requested
to provide any proposed 2024 budget amendments to the City Clerk by Monday, December 9th
to be included on the agenda. No proposed budget amendments were received by the City Clerk.
Therefore, Budget 2025 is, as per provincial legislation, considered adopted as of this date.
However, as we did last year, we will formally receive it a little later this afternoon and direct staff to implement it.
Colleagues, while this seems like a brief exercise in following legislative requirements,
I must take a moment to recognize that we arrived at this place because of the thorough, professional and responsive work of staff
to balance providing services that Kitchener residents and businesses rely on with prudent
fiscal management. Having had the benefit of experiencing budget
processes in more than one municipality during my time in an elected office, I have come
to appreciate, especially this year, the professionalism, dedication, collaboration and thorough approach
led by Dan Chapner, our C.A.O., Jonathan Lautenbach, our C.F.O., our corporate leadership team,
finance budget team and the many staff who are part of Team Kitchener and each year help build
a budget for the residents and businesses in our community. I want to again acknowledge and thank
both Councillor Scott Davey and Bill Dionitis, Chair and Vice Chair respectively, for their
leadership and support in this work and all of Council for the engagement throughout the process.
I'd now like to share again some of the comments that Chair Davey made on my behalf when tabling
the budget. The 2025 draft budget was prepared by staff and presented for Council's consideration
built on the success of previous budget by continuing to address priorities that are
important for Kitchener and its residents. From delivering the programs and services that residents
and businesses rely on every day, to investments in infrastructure that help to address the city's
asset replacement and growth related needs, to providing funding to implement the city's 20 to
2023 to 2026 strategic plan that will help shape Kitchener's future. The 2025 final budget balances
several priorities and continues the trend of delivering good value for Kitchener residents.
With a proposed tax increase of 3.9% as outlined in the budget, we continue to maintain existing
service levels for the approximately 50 core services that the City provides,
and while still responding to growth related pressures that come with
welcoming new residents to Kitchener each year. The budget also ensures that
Kitchener's average property tax increase over 10 years remains below
Ontario's inflation rate increases during the same time period. Our city has
continued to grow over the past many years and is now home to over 300,000
residents. Even with the increased pressures of serving a larger population
base, the City has been able to keep pace, carefully balancing increasing service needs
while still proposing budget increases that we believe are reasonable. Kitchener's tax levy
per capita is one of the lowest in the province when compared to other large municipalities in
Ontario, and it also has what's considered a low municipal burden when combining both taxes and
utility rates and comparing Kitchener to other municipalities. Kitchener's track record speaks
for itself when it comes to balancing affordability, service demands, and responding to growth-related
pressures. I'm proud of this Council and staff's approach to rate setting and believe Kitchener
is a model of efficient, effective, and sustainable local government. As was stated, during the past
10 years, Kitchener's tax rate increases have averaged 2.47%, below the Ontario inflation,
which has averaged 2.64% during that same time frame. This should give residents confidence
that they're getting good value for the programs and services that the City provides. Kitchener is
also making important investments in infrastructure, recognizing the need to take care of the $10
billion worth of assets that the City is responsible for, while also moving forward with new
infrastructure that's needed to support housing and a growing community. Besides the City's own
efforts and strategies to try and address capital funding needs, staff have also pursued federal
and provincial grant opportunities, successfully securing over $200 million in federal and provincial
funding over the past five years. I want to thank and acknowledge both our federal and our provincial
partners for their support of these initiatives over time. As the City continues to expand,
particularly in the southwest area, new amenities are needed to support recreational needs,
and this budget reflects those investments.
This includes $16 million for the construction of a new library branch in Southwest Kitchener
that will be fully operational in 2025,
$6 million for the Rosenberg Community Centre that will provide programming space for the surrounding neighbourhood,
and $144 million for the Kitchener Indoor Recreation Facility that will be located at Schlegel Park
and is currently under construction with an indoor pool, FIFA-sized soccer facility
and will provide other important gathering spaces for residents and the community.
Finally, our community is in the second year of implementation of its 2023-2026 strategic plan.
The 2025 budget continues to build on investments made through last year's budget process
while funding with funding allocated within the budget to support actions identified under the
five goal areas within the plan including building a connected city together, cultivating a green city
together, creating an economically thriving city together, fostering a caring city together,
and stewarding a better city together. The 2025 budget highlights approximately $75 million in
funding that will help to advance strategic priorities and this includes $56 million in
federal and provincial funding that the City has received to help advance affordable housing
initiatives. Some of these investments in other important areas include $8.6 million towards
advancing actions in the City's parks master plan including improvements being made at Upper Canada
and McLennan Park, $1.3 million towards implementation of the City Tree Canopy Plan,
$800,000 in green fleet improvements including the replacement of three ice resurfacers to electric,
$780,000 in operating and capital funding to support the activation of the Conrad Centre,
and $100,000 to increase spots in summer camps for youth. These examples and more build on
progress made in the previous year helping Kitchener deliver on key priorities and commitments
including our strategic plan. I'm pleased with where we've landed with the 2025 budget for the
progressive actions that we continue to take to the City to move us closer to achieving our vision
while still balancing affordability and operational service delivery needs. Once again I want to thank
this Council for your ongoing leadership of this community, our corporate leadership team for the
fantastic leadership that they provide throughout the organization and and very
importantly in this process our finance budget team without whose leadership and
support budgets like this would not be possible thank you to everyone and with
